  • Attorney general says E1 settlement decision should not be taken by caretaker government led by Netanyahu.
  • Israel has postponed issuing contracts for the construction of a large settlement on the West Bank seen as likely to render a two-state solution unviable, days after the UK imposed sanctions against building firms operating in the area.
  • Israeli diplomats insisted the move was not in response to the measures from Downing Street.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Attorney general says E1 settlement decision should not be taken by caretaker government led by Netanyahu.

Israel has postponed issuing contracts for the construction of a large settlement on the West Bank seen as likely to render a two-state solution unviable, days after the UK imposed sanctions against building firms operating in the area.

Israeli diplomats insisted the move was not in response to the measures from Downing Street. Gali Baharav-Miara, the attorney general, noted any decision on settlement expansion should not be taken by the caretaker government led by Benjamin Netanyahu but by whatever latest administration was formed.

She ordered the Israel land authority and ministry of housing not to open the tender process. Israeli diplomats suggested the UK foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, had acted prematurely on Monday in sanctioning the eight construction firms. But UK diplomats believe the growing political pressure on Israel over settlements, including from US Democrats, is having an impact.

The deferral puts the E1 settlement expansion in the mix for any coalition negotiations. The leader of the Change bloc, Gadi Eisenkot, seen as Israel’s most likely next prime minister, has been clear in opposing violent settler activity, as has the newly elected Knesset speaker, Matan Kahana, an ally of Eisenkot.

Eisenkot has also opposed the E1 settlement expansion, describing it as a mistake likely to alienate international opinion. He remarked of the plan: “I recall that Netanyahu himself opposed this for a long time, and due to coalition pressure, he gave in and approved it.”.

The EI settlement expansion, due to have been announced on Thursday, has long been seen as qualitatively different since the land – between Jerusalem and Ma’aleh Adumim, a West Bank settlement city of nearly 40,000 residents – bisects the West Bank and cuts it off from East Jerusalem.

Industry observers note that miliband has noted it would mark the death knell of a future Palestinian state. The UK, along with a group of European countries, has recently recognised Palestine, and the preservation of a two-state solution has been described as the north star of Labour policy towards the region.

The construction tender was published for more than 3,401 housing units in the area. At the beginning of November, the Israel Defense Forces began demolishing homes in a Bedouin community within the E1 area.

Israel has already enforced the downgrading of the UK consulate in East Jerusalem as a reprisal for Miliband’s decision in September to try to end trade links with the illegal settlements.

Bennett stated: “The British Labour government’s hostility, bias and one-sided approach are particularly glaring given its failure to take any action against the Palestinian Authority, which continues to encourage terrorism through financial payments, promote incitement in its education system and engage in illegal construction in violation of signed agreements.”.

Although the Israeli election was largely fought on domestic security-related concerns, Eisenkot seems to be more sensitive to the implications of Israel’s crumbling global reputation, and the need to make efforts to be seen to be listening to the criticism.

If he becomes prime minister, Eisenkot will, indirectly at least, also have to take account of the views of the Arab parties even if these parties are not going to become members of the government.

The group Peace Now welcomed the attorney general’s decision: “A government that lost the elections is not permitted to exploit its final days in power to advance destructive moves that will endanger Israel’s future and its international standing.

According to recent reports, construction in E1 is liable to eliminate the possibility of a two-state solution and drag Israel into a severe diplomatic crisis and international sanctions. The AG’s decision is an key step, but the struggle is not over yet.”.

  • It has been revealed that in the last few months, Wiltschko claims, Osmo’s model has achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence.” The company’s definition of this is that the model is about as good as the average person at detecting and discriminating between smells, and about as good as a junior perfume designer at creating them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that in a lab near Newark Airport in Newly introduced Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation model for smell. The organization’s goal, indicates founder Alex Wiltschko, is “to give computers a sense of smell.”.

“Scent molecules are really the only language most species on this planet can speak,” he says. “Most species can’t communicate with sound or visually, so it truly is Earth’s original language. And it’s incredibly powerful for us, from a memory and an emotional standpoint. You can smell something once and remember it for the rest of your life. You can smell something on the street and be pulled back to high school.”.

It has been revealed that in the last few months, Wiltschko claims, Osmo’s model has achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence.” The company’s definition of this is that the model is about as good as the average person at detecting and discriminating between smells, and about as good as a junior perfume designer at creating them. It says its technology is already being used in the fragrance industry to help brands design and manufacture new scents. Last month, the company says, Osmo’s AI model outperformed in-house perfumers at one of the world’s largest consumer goods companies. Wiltschko believes it could be deployed eventually for threat detection at airports, for example, or diagnosing diseases.

In a recent development, wiltschko spun the startup out of his work at Google Brain, the search giant’s former AI research lab, in 2023, and he is running the same playbook as AI startups in other domains: Throw a lot of data at difficult problems, and see what happens. The challenge with scent, Wiltschko indicates, is that there was a dearth of good data. Before Osmo, there were fewer than 200,000 human descriptions of smells in existing databases, by his count. Plus, the chemical sensor devices needed to collect data are expensive, and the fragrance industry is secretive about its work on olfactory science.

A lot of the manufacturer’s work has been in creating its own dataset of more than 10 million human labels and 800 million “scent tokens,” which describe the exact molecules and concentrations that go into creating specific odors. Osmo uses spectrometers and other chemical sensors, running around the clock, to break down the molecular makeup of everything from fruit and flowers to pantry  staples and organs. A team of around 70 trained data labelers in the US and overseas spend their days sniffing things and writing down what they smell like, using a standardized fragrance vocabulary.

In a recent development, mapping out scents in this way is throwing out some unlikely parallels. In the same way that changing the order of words can drastically influence the meaning of a sentence, rearranging scent molecules in different proportions can drastically alter the smells humans perceive. “The scent tokens that define the smell of a newborn baby have massive overlap with the scent tokens in a fresh plate of cooked spaghetti,” Wiltschko claims. (Specifically Barilla brand spaghetti, he says, which perhaps raises some questions for the people at the pasta factory.).

It has been revealed that the tech giant also creates its own scents, using a smell-printing robot the size of a school bus that mixes ingredients according to precise formulas to make samples for Osmo’s own research and fragrances for paying customers. It can design and print scents to order based on a ChatGPT-style prompt. Wiltschko flipped open his laptop to show me how the AI model worked. He opened a text box on screen, and I asked him to generate a fragrance that smelled like a Portuguese custard tart (we were in Lisbon for Web Summit), aimed at 18- to 23-year-old men. The system spent a few minutes cogitating, then generated three options for potential scent profiles that matched the brief (creamy, coconutty, fruity) and the molecules needed to create them. If I’d continued with the ordering process, my signature L’Eau de Custard would have been ready about a week later.

Osmo’s technology has already been used to create retail fragrances, including for giants like Procter & Gamble. The Gates Foundation, which invested $5 million when Osmo launched, later gave the firm a $3.5 million grant to assess molecules that repel disease-carrying insects, and Osmo identified eight substances that were more repellent than DEET. Osmo has also worked with StockX, the online clothing marketplace, on using smell to spot counterfeit sneakers by detecting differences in the chemical composition of the materials used in the shoes.

But not everyone is convinced by the technology or the organization’s significant claims. Avery Gilbert, a smell scientist and author of What the Nose Knows, has been sharply critical of Osmo on his Substack, arguing that some of its marketing claims are undocumented, and that its patent filings still rely on human sensory panels and perfumers, rather than AI. “This heavy reliance on human sensory judgments seems odd for a company premised on super-cool AI,” he wrote in March. In response, Wiltschko indicates that “human perception isn't a workaround for AI”. “Language models learn from what people have written. Our model learns from what people smell. Smell is ultimately a human experience, so the model has to learn from humans to bridge chemistry and perception. That’s what lets it predict how people will experience a scent as well as the human nose does.”.

Sources indicate that michael Schmuker, a former professor of neural computation at the University of Hertfordshire who has previously consulted for Osmo, says the firm’s technology is an achievement. With colleagues, he created an open-source, reverse-engineered version of Osmo’s 2023 model, but it lacks the reams of data the company has collected since.

But even with all this smell data, Osmo may be missing some of the factors that make human olfaction unique, Schmuker says. “Smell is super complex. Context is very notable for smell. The same molecule may evoke a different association depending on context,” he says. “[The smell of] a French cheese like Camembert is partly the same molecule as in used nappies. You don’t confuse the two because of the context.”.

It has been revealed that in a controlled setting like a fragrance lab, this lack of context may not matter so much. But it could have an impact if Osmo’s technology becomes, as Wiltschko suggests, the “olfactive channel” for AI world models. Imagine a machine that could sniff out spoilage in food on a production line, or detect tumors through smell the way dogs have been trained to do in pilot studies.

For that to happen, sensor technology will need to get a lot better, Schmuker notes. The models will need to keep improving. Medical diagnostics is the biggest prize.

“There’s a lot of history of companies that have gone directly at that mountain peak and, unfortunately, not been successful, because it is very expensive and it is very difficult,” Wiltschko says. "So what we’re doing is building this foundation at the foothills of all these mountains. We’re sending expeditions up to the mountains, doing explorations, and basically smelling the whole world.”.

Industry News: The Boox Picco made me love tiny e-readers

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (796 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I don't get the hype of tiny e-readers.
  • Boox is one of the first big brands to launch a mini e-reader of its own, the Picco.
  • The physical design of the Boox Picco isn't all that different from other tiny e-readers, but what matters is literally what's on the inside.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I don't get the hype of tiny e-readers. I've used a ton of e-readers — Kindles, Kobos, and Boox — and I thought they were just the right size, and I wasn't craving a smaller e-reader. But plenty of people clearly are, as I've spent hours browsing Reddit and reading about how people use their tiny e-readers.

Boox is one of the first big brands to launch a mini e-reader of its own, the Picco. Other Boox e-readers run on Android, but the Picco does not. I expected to be underwhelmed, but I'm glad to be wrong. The Boox Picco has given me a whole latest love for tiny e-readers, and I finally understand their appeal.

The physical design of the Boox Picco isn't all that different from other tiny e-readers, but what matters is literally what's on the inside. The user interface is exceptionally easy to navigate and straightforward — it's pretty pared back compared to Kindle or Kobo.

According to recent reports, the Picco combines physical buttons and touchscreen controls. The 'bookshelf' section is the device's native library. 'Transfer' lets you move books from the Boox Tile app on your phone to the device; 'Apps' offers a limited selection of pre-downloaded apps; and 'Settings' is exactly as it says. You can even set any photo as your lock screen, but keep in mind that the Boox Picco display is black-and-white only.

Recent findings suggest that you can easily move to the home screen by swiping up, and swipe down to adjust brightness and warmth. Plus, it has two side buttons, which serve as page-turn buttons. The Pico is super responsive and loads pages quickly. I was worried I'd get overwhelmed by all the controls, but it's so intuitive that I quickly took to it and was navigating like it was second nature.

It has been revealed that there isn't much to navigate on the device, but that's part of what makes it so easy. It's all about keeping you focused with apps like a to-do list and a Pomodoro timer.

If you've used other e-readers, you might be used to devices from the same brand speaking to each other. So Boox e-reader owners might expect the Picco to sync with other Boox models. Unfortunately, that's not the case. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

The Boox Picco only connects to WiFi temporarily to transfer files. Since it doesn't maintain a connection, it won't frequently update to reflect whatever's in your Boox library. This also means that it won't update your progress in a book across e-readers, so you'll have to manually turn the page to catch up when you switch devices.

Industry observers note that with a 3.97-inch screen, it's an incredibly small e-reader designed to literally fit on the back of your phone. While other tiny e-readers have promised the same, the Boox Picco really does. Its MagSafe case is perfectly positioned so it attaches conveniently without hanging off the side. Keep in mind, though, it fits best on an iPhone Pro Max (pictured below).

In a recent development, it feels very sturdy, too, living up to its $110 price tag. Weighing two ounces, it has a slight heft so it doesn't feel like it'll slip out of your hand, but it also doesn't add too much weight to your phone when attached.

Tiny e-readers have one massive overarching issue, so this isn't exclusive to the Boox Picco, but you're only able to read DRM-free EPUB files. Typically, these e-books are only in the public domain, so you're extremely limited in what you can read on the device. That means any EPUBs you borrowed on Libby or purchased on Kindle or Kobo can't be uploaded to the Boox Picco.

So, for most e-reader owners, the Boox Picco won't align with their reading habits.

Industry observers note that yes, the Boox Picco is the tiny e-reader worth buying — although it won't be for everyone. You need to temper your expectations about what you can read on it, as it only supports DRM-free EPUBs. But if you're reading DRM-free EPUBs on your e-reader anyway, then the Boox Picco is a fun device to add to your repertoire.

Industry observers note that it's well-designed inside and out, with a sturdy case that snaps onto MagSafe devices, and an easy-to-navigate user interface. At $109.99, it's cheaper than most e-readers we've tested, which feels on par for a device that is smaller and possesses fewer capabilities than a standard e-reader. And if you're deciding between an Xteink e-reader and the Boox Picco — go for the Picco. It's far more user-friendly.

MAHA PAC spent more on steak, luxury club than candidates, report reveals

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (575 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the wake of the Make America Healthy Again movement’s midterm wipeout, a top leader suggested the heavy losses came down to being outspent by wealthier, more powerful rivals.
  • The dive into the financial documents reveals that the MAHA PAC, led by Tony Lyons, spent more on allies, boosters, meals, luxuries, and its affiliated nonprofit than it did on political candidates.
  • Industry observers note that the findings are in stark contrast to an announcement from Lyons in the spring that he was heading a $100 million fundraiser to boost MAHA’s clout in the midterms.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the wake of the Make America Healthy Again movement’s midterm wipeout, a top leader suggested the heavy losses came down to being outspent by wealthier, more powerful rivals. But a Stat report on MAHA’s own spending in the run-up to the election raises questions about whether the group’s priority was ever winning elections in the first place.

The dive into the financial documents reveals that the MAHA PAC, led by Tony Lyons, spent more on allies, boosters, meals, luxuries, and its affiliated nonprofit than it did on political candidates.

Industry observers note that the findings are in stark contrast to an announcement from Lyons in the spring that he was heading a $100 million fundraiser to boost MAHA’s clout in the midterms. In reality, MAHA PAC took in $3.2 million. During the election cycle, the PAC spent more than $10.5 million, with over $7 million coming from money it had collected previously.

According to Stat’s findings, of the $10.5 million the MAHA PAC spent on the midterms, less than a tenth—roughly $1 million—went to messaging on political candidates, which are expenses called “independent expenditures.”.

Andrew Mayersohn, a committees researcher at OpenSecrets, called the spending “pretty unusual,” explaining that “Major super PACs spend most of their money on independent expenditures.”.

It has been revealed that in some cases, the scant political spending was dwarfed by spending on luxuries. For instance, in a key House race in Northern California, MAHA supported Kevin Kiley over his political rival, pediatrician Richard Pan. Despite calling the race “the most direct ideological confrontation” between MAHA and its opposition “anywhere on the 2026 ballot,” the PAC only spent $49,900 to back Kiley. That’s a little less than the $50,100 it spent at Mastro’s Steakhouse, an upscale restaurant that offers $110 porterhouse steaks in Washington, DC. Further, it’s less than a third of the $155,900 the PAC spent at Ned’s Club, a luxury club near the White House that has become a popular gathering spot among Trump officials.

Kiley lost the election to Pan by double digits.

Of the roughly $1 million spent on political candidates, most of it—over $700,000—went to defeating Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-La.). Many other MAHA-endorsed candidates received $50,000 or less. Some got less than $2,000.

According to recent reports, outside of steaks and a private club, the MAHA PAC spent $500,000 on a media tech giant, Merit Street Media, run by Phil McGraw, who hosted a MAHA special featuring Dr. Phil. MAHA leaders used PAC money to cover meals, payroll, and credit card bills. The PAC paid $275,000 to a security firm, Gavin de Becker & Associates, which is led by an ally of anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., MAHA’s top leader. Tens of thousands more went to LLCs that have little to no online information.

Industry observers note that on the other hand, prominent online MAHA influencers also pocketed tens of thousands from the PAC, as did writers for The MAHA Report, a Substack that promotes Kennedy and MAHA interests. In the days after the midterms, as members of the movement were coming to grips with the election losses, The MAHA Report chose to publish a lengthy article defending convicted rapist Russel Brand, a Kennedy ally who became a MAHA fixture.

The biggest chunk of the MAHA PAC’s spending—more than $3 million—went to the nonprofit MAHA Action, which is also run by Lyons. It’s unclear how all that money was spent.

Rejecting cheap fabrics, higher prices: Why shoppers are asking for better clothes

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1284 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Clothing isn't made like it used to be, and more shoppers are taking notice.
  • It has been revealed that the makeup of apparel imported into the U.S.
  • Industry observers note that apparel prices generally declined over the two decades leading up to the pandemic, according to the consumer price index.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Clothing isn't made like it used to be, and more shoppers are taking notice.

It has been revealed that the makeup of apparel imported into the U.S. has shifted in recent years. In 2010, about 60% of clothing was predominantly made from cotton. Now, that total is around 45%, while predominantly synthetic fabrics such as polyester and nylon comprise the majority of imports.

Industry observers note that apparel prices generally declined over the two decades leading up to the pandemic, according to the consumer price index. Since 2020, they have soared to record highs.

It's starting to change habits for consumers who are paying more for food, gas, rent and other staples. As shoppers shell out more for clothes, they're increasingly making sure the garments are worth the cost.

Consulting firm AlixPartners' 2026 Consumer Sentiment Index, which surveyed more than 9,000 shoppers, found that consumers are scrutinizing labels more closely and rejecting cheap materials sold at a premium.

"If it's not a natural material, a retailer brand who passes it off as it is, they're really becoming very low on consumers' minds," noted Sonia Lapinsky, head of fashion at AlixPartners.

Fast fashion brands like Forever 21 and H&M exploded in popularity during the early 2000s and 2010s, bringing trendy clothing to shelves rapidly at low prices. Then came ultra-fast fashion, with brands like Shein and Fashion Nova pumping out fresh garments at even quicker speeds and lower price points — made possible in part through the use of inexpensive, synthetic fabrics.

Recent findings suggest that "We got to a point where the pendulum just swung too far in that direction. And we've actually begun to see a reversal," said U.S. Bancorp BTIG consumer analyst Janine Stichter. "Quality matters a lot more ... over the last three or four years than it has in the previous 10 or 20.".

But quality, which shoppers often tie directly to material, can come at a higher cost.

In a recent development, the average unit price of apparel imported to the U.S. between January and August was $2.64 per square meter for garments that were predominantly synthetic fiber, like polyester and nylon, compared with $3.67 for items that were largely cotton, according to data from the U.S. Commerce Department's Office of Textiles and Apparel.

When comparing those 2026 figures to 2010, synthetic fiber apparel import costs have climbed around 11%, while cotton apparel costs have risen 21%.

"If you're appealing to a more value-sensitive customer, you either reduce the quality, or you negotiate with suppliers to try to share some of the cost or you maybe absorb the cost … and perhaps hope to crank a higher volume of product to make up for it," mentioned Bernstein Research senior retail analyst Aneesha Sherman.

In a recent development, though polyester is cheaper, experts point out that's not necessarily a bad thing. It can help clothing hold its shape and wick away sweat.

Sherman believes the athleisure boom is a primary factor in the shift toward polyester. She stated that from 2015 to 2025, sports apparel was growing at a 4.9% rate in the U.S., versus 2.6% for all apparel and footwear, according to Euromonitor data.

"There probably is some quality trade down as well happening there," Sherman stated. "But I think both these trends are conflated.".

Nonetheless, backlash to synthetic materials is growing. Gen Z has even repurposed the word "polyester" as an insult to mean generally low-quality or fake.

Concerns have also grown about the environment and human health surrounding petroleum-based clothing, as more research indicates microplastics can leach from polyester clothing when washed.

It's led consumers to reexamine what materials are in their clothing.

Apparel prices have risen coming out of the pandemic, as demand outpaced supply and allowed companies to raise prices, remarked BTIG's Stichter. Tariffs and the Iran war followed, raising costs for businesses — and prices for consumers.

Petroleum is the basis of many synthetic fibers, and oil prices have skyrocketed since the start of the Iran war.

The same factors that helped drive up prices of clothing — Covid, tariffs and war — also affected clothing quality.

"Companies had to move around their supply chains in the post-Covid period," said Stichter. "They had to find ways to take costs out, and sometimes that meant using less expensive fabrics.".

Those factors compounded a more-than-decade-long shift away from manufacturing in China.

Sheng Lu, a fashion and apparel studies professor at the University of Delaware, whose research focuses on the economics of the global textile industry, stated China's established history with clothing production means it has higher-skilled workers, state-of-the-art-equipment and better material management compared with emerging manufacturing destinations such as Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Cambodia.

Sources indicate that "They mostly serve the value market and the mass market. And I think the reason why they're not ready to make higher-quality luxury and premium products really reflects the kind of skill sets you can expect when you source from these countries," said Lu.

AlixPartners' Lapinsky mentioned these countries that manufacture at a lower cost sometimes have to still ship the raw materials from China, which can extend the timeline to make clothing. That means taking earlier bets on trends and then discounting if products don't sell well.

"If you have to mark down that product because the consumer doesn't want it as much, your net margin might actually be worse than if you were to just invest in quality in the first place," noted BTIG's Stichter.

And as material costs rise for synthetic fibers, Stichter also remarked she believes it could further influence companies to use more natural fabrics moving forward.

Companies prioritizing quality are winning in this environment.

According to recent reports, ralph Lauren's stock is up around 85% over the past two years. Around 90% of its apparel is primarily made of cotton, leather, wool, viscose, cashmere or silk, according to its 2026 sustainability report. In its fiscal 2026, the company said it sold more products at full price and reduced markdowns.

Meanwhile, direct-to-consumer clothing brand Quince, which centers its brand identity around natural materials, reached a $10 billion valuation this year.

Industry observers note that the brand jumped 16 spots to No. 3 for best resale value in online consignment retailer ThredUp's 2025 report. Organic cotton retailer Pact jumped 20 spots on that list to No. 8, illustrating the potential role materials are playing in brand recognition.

Industry observers note that alternatively, the 2026 AlixPartners report, which ranks sentiment for brands in different retail categories, found shoppers are viewing some fast fashion brands less favorably. Both Shein and Zara dropped three spots — to fifth and seventh place, respectively — in terms of sentiment in the young adult specialty category.

Shein passed higher tariff costs onto shoppers in 2025 and then blamed a sales slowdown on those higher prices. The ultra-fast fashion retailer saw its year-over-year share of U.S. apparel, accessories and footwear card spending decrease in the fourth quarter of 2025 and first two quarters of 2026, according to Consumer Edge.

Shein did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Though Zara fell in AlixPartners' Consumer Sentiment Index, it has continued to grow sales and profits year over year. Even so, Lapinsky remarked worsening consumer views are something to watch, even if the firm is doing well.

"What we found over the years with this consumer sentiment index is that sometimes it will be a bit of a leading indicator of what's to come," said AlixPartners' Lapinsky. "I'm not saying that this is going to be true for Zara, but I think that's one thing that we'll be watching as we look in the upcoming quarters and into 2027.".

UK anti-migrant activist jailed for slashing Channel dinghy

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A British anti-migrant activist has been sentenced to 15 months in prison for slashing a dinghy used by migrants crossing the English Channel while a French rescue worker was still on board.
  • In a recent development, daniel Thomas, 37, also known as "Danny Tommo," pleaded guilty to criminal damage earlier this month.
  • The activist, who founded the anti-immigration group Patriot Platform, livestreamed the September 22 incident on social media, where it was watched by a large audience.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A British anti-migrant activist has been sentenced to 15 months in prison for slashing a dinghy used by migrants crossing the English Channel while a French rescue worker was still on board.

In a recent development, daniel Thomas, 37, also known as "Danny Tommo," pleaded guilty to criminal damage earlier this month. He was sentenced on Friday at Portsmouth Crown Court in southern England.

The activist, who founded the anti-immigration group Patriot Platform, livestreamed the September 22 incident on social media, where it was watched by a large audience.

Thomas had followed an inflatable boat carrying dozens of migrants across the Channel on September 22.

After the migrants were transferred to another vessel and taken ashore, Thomas approached the empty dinghy, which a French rescue worker had boarded.

Industry observers note that video footage highlighted him repeatedly stabbing the boat with a knife. Judge James Newton-Price mentioned he counted eight cuts.

During the livestream, Thomas could be heard saying "this is what needs to happen.".

He also shouted "get off the boat, you've got time to get off the boat ... take them back, no more of these," according to prosecutor Joel Smith.

It has been revealed that newton-Price accepted that there was "no immediate danger" to the rescue worker. However, he stated Thomas' aggressive behavior would have been highly alarming.

Sentencing Thomas, Newton-Price mentioned his actions amounted to "flagrant interference and a deliberate disruption" of the legitimate activities of British and French authorities in the Channel.

The judge highlighted the work of Britain's Border Force, Coastguard and volunteers from the Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI).

"They do necessary, highly sensitive and difficult jobs, and which should not be disrupted by a publicity-seeker slashing with a knife a boat they were attempting to recover," he noted.

Thomas appeared by videolink from a prison in Winchester, southern England, where he has been held since late September after being denied bail.

He reportedly held his head in his hands when the sentence was declared.

Under current UK sentencing rules, Thomas may serve only a third of his 15-month sentence, including time already spent in custody.

The court also heard that he had five previous convictions, including one for kidnapping in 2016.

Thomas is a longtime ally of prominent far-right activist Tommy Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon.

He has built a large online following and founded Patriot Platform, a group campaigning against migrants arriving in Britain in small boats.

Thomas gained prominence earlier this year by leading confrontational anti-migrant demonstrations in Portsmouth and the southeastern port of Dover.

Hundreds of protesters, many dressed in black and wearing face coverings, blocked roads and clashed with police.

The demonstrations have increasingly targeted police officers and rescue workers involved in responding to migrant boats arriving on British shores.

The UK government has condemned the protesters' "intimidating and thuggish behavior.".

Thomas is also due to stand trial in London next June over several alleged offenses, including entering a restricted zone at a migrant processing center in Dover in March.

Successive British governments have struggled to stop migrants from making the dangerous journey across the English Channel, one of the world's busiest shipping lanes.

More than 41,000 people crossed the Channel in small boats last year.

Although the number of arrivals has since fallen, the crossings remain a major political concern in Britain.

Right-wing opposition parties and anti-immigration campaigners have continued to demand tougher measures to prevent migrants from reaching the country.

It has been revealed that you want an e-reader that does more: If you want to do more on an e-reader, like check your Storygraph or browse Libby, then you'll need one with an open system. The Boox Go 6 (Gen II) runs on an Android 11 system with access to the Google Play Store, so you can download any app to your e-reader. Yes, it could lead to more distractions, but with an E Ink display, it still feels more analog than a classic iPad or Android tablet.

But you want it to look like an e-reader: The Boox Go 6 (Gen II) doesn't look like a tablet, though. The E Ink display provides a matte, black and white background with 300 ppi resolution, so it's gentle on the eyes. It's the same size as a basic Kindle but with the flush front design of a Paperwhite, so it gives you the best of both worlds.

The Boox Go 6 (Gen II) is the brand's answer to Amazon's Kindle. With a 6-inch screen, it fits comfortably in your hand for hours of reading. With an open Android system, you can download any app in the Google Play Store, so you can access any book across any app, including Kindle, Rakuten Kobo, and Libby.

It's the perfect size and shape to hold for hours at a time. Boox even sells a MagSafe case so you can pop on a PopSockets grip for an ergonomic hold. Boox e-readers do have a bit of a learning curve, as the E Ink display requires a bit of tinkering. But once you get it set up, it's extremely customizable.

Because it can tackle a lot of apps rather than just doing one thing like a Kindle, it needs some extra power behind it. Unfortunately, it doesn't quite have it. The Boox Go 6 suffers from significant lag and screen response complications that make it occasionally frustrating to use. It's slower than either a Kindle or a Kobo, but it's a consolation you'll have to make if you want an e-reader that does more.

In a recent development, miniature enthusiasts: If you want an e-reader that you can have on you at all times and even slip in your pocket, there are so few options out there. That's what makes the Xetink X4 so special. It's a truly tiny e-reader with a 4.3-inch display; but with a built-in magnet, it can attach to MagSafe devices so you can keep it attached to your iPhone.

Sources indicate that you must love DRM ePUBs: If you think you're getting a mini Kindle, you're not. Instead, expect a tiny e-reader that is a great fit for turning online articles into PDFs or collecting all the free ePUBs. It's not compatible with any DRM files.

In such a little package, the Xetink X4 feels like it should be a toy, but it's actually a solid e-reader. It's the smallest e-reader we've tested, measuring 4.3 inches, so you can slip it in your pocket and go. That small display, while convenient on the go, won't be suitable for all eyes, especially if you like to crank up the text size on your e-reader or phone.

In a recent development, the resolution of the Xetink X4 is 219 ppi, which is lower res than you'll find on most e-readers. It also includes page-turning buttons along the bottom of the e-reader. Xteink has a great transfer system, too. It's similar to Amazon's Send to Kindle feature, in that you can send EPUBs and articles to the e-reader. The ability to send articles is particularly compelling, so you can send your reading list to your e-reader and enjoy them in one spot.

My biggest issue with the Xetink X4 is how few files it supports, as you can't access Libby books or any DRM files on it. In a recent development, quality on a budget: If you want to dip your toes into e-readers, the standard Kindle model is the best budget-friendly model. Amazon made some updates to the 2026 Kindle that make it worthy of its higher price tag. It has a new, flush front design for a sleeker look. It's a speedy little e-reader, too. Its screen is responsive and loads books within seconds. The only thing that could make the e-reader better is if Amazon added an adjustable warm light and made it waterproof. However, according to Amazon, the lack of those features keeps it affordable.

The device is now available in its basic format in either ube or graphite. However, it's also available with an aluminum backing, making it more like a tablet. The aluminum Kindle is more expensive at $189.99, but it does come with 32GB of storage and two additional color options.

Sources indicate that above all, the Kobo Libra Colour has the best ergonomic design. It's more square than a Kindle, as one side offers extra space for page-turning buttons. Recent findings suggest that young readers: If you're raising a voracious reader, the Kindle Paperwhite Kids is the best e-reader for kids. One area where Amazon has all other e-reader brands beat is in the kids market. There are special kid-friendly models of the basic Kindle, Kindle Paperwhite, and Kindle Colorsoft. Our preferred model for kids is the Kindle Paperwhite Kids.

Recent findings suggest that more than anything else, an e-reader for kids has to be waterproof, which is why the Kindle Paperwhite Kids is the best choice. I enjoyed writing with the pen, and I swear my handwriting looked better on the Kindle Scribe than on my iPad.

Recent findings suggest that it finally got a processing patch that makes it as speedy as every other Kindle. Gone is the lag when switching between journals and books. It's not your only option if you want a Kindle that can write. The Scribe Colorsoft is also available, and while we appreciate that model, it's quite a bit more expensive. The 2025 Scribe is a better value; it just doesn't have the wow factor of color.

Single device users: There are so many devices that the modern person is meant to have. If adding an e-reader seems superfluous, I'd recommend a tablet that allows you to read books, stream highlights, and browse the internet. The best tablet for reading? It's the iPad mini.

According to recent reports, but why is this iPad better than any other? It's all about the size. At 8.3 inches, it comfortably sits in your hand and is about the same size as a paperback.

In a recent development, before testing these e-readers, I read using my 9th-generation iPad, and my main complaint was always the size. After 30 minutes of reading, my hand and wrist would strain holding up all 10.2 inches of the screen. That's why the 8.3-inch display of the iPad mini was such a treat. Reading with the mini made me feel like I was holding an actual book rather than a laptop screen.

It has been revealed that unsurprisingly, the iPad mini has the most computing power of all the e-readers on this list. It jumps between apps and turns pages without an ounce of hesitation. Plus, it offers the most expansive ways to read books. You can read using Apple's built-in Apple Books app or download and read within the Kindle and Libby apps. And unlike most e-readers, you can read comics and graphic novels in full color. Plus, it has far more storage than any other e-reader, as the 7th generation iPad mini starts at 128GB of storage.

Recent findings suggest that despite my love of the iPad mini, I have some beef, most of which is with the screen. While I love its overall size, it has a substantial glare problem. I've found this to be true with any iPad I've read on; the slick glass screen has a glare in almost any environment. That's no surprise in the sun, but even at night, I found the screen to be a little too shiny, causing my eyes to have some trouble focusing. This does have a fix; if you want your iPad screen to look more like the matte of a Kindle, a screen protector such as Paperlike creates that effect.

Additionally, compared to e-readers, which provide months of battery life, the iPad mini only gets you hours. If you're reading for a couple of hours a day, you're probably only charging the iPad once a week, which isn't a big deal but certainly more than a traditional e-reader.

Onyx Boox Go 7: While we love the Boox Go 6, we didn't love the Go 7. It's the same size as the Kobo Libra or Amazon Kindle, but it really lags on processing speed. According to recent reports, in terms of substantial-name e-readers, you might notice one omission from this list: the Barnes & Noble Nook. However, unless you are a loyal buyer of Barnes & Noble books, I recommend steering clear of the Nook.

Once you get an e-reader, it's time to fill it up with books, and that doesn't necessarily mean spending money. In fact, you can load up your e-reader without spending a dime; you just need to be a bit resourceful.

The best way to read nearly any book — a classic or hot newly introduced release — is with Libby. I have read hundreds of free books with the Libby app — I wouldn't have been able to test for this guide without it. It connects with your library card, allowing you to borrow from your local library's digital collection. Plus, both Kobo and Kindle have exceptional Libby integrations.

Another way to build your library is through Stuff Your Kindle Day events. These are 24-hour opportunities led by authors that make books discounted or free.

If you're a fan of the classics or looking to discover a treasure lost to time, an online resource like Project Gutenberg has more than 75,000 books in the public domain that you can download and read on an e-reader.

Industry observers note that the best Kindle is the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition, dethroning the standard Paperwhite. Overall, it strikes the right balance of performance and value, while possessing everything we want in an e-reader. The standard Kindle is great for those on a budget, but it's not waterproof, and while the basic Paperwhite is always a favorite, the Signature Edition aluminum case and extra features make it the best e-reader you can buy.

It has been revealed that our two favorite e-readers come from Kindle and Kobo, but is one better than the other? It depends on what you're looking for. If performance is your primary concern, then a Kindle, specifically the Paperwhite, is better as it outperforms the Kobo Libra Colour in terms of speed when turning pages or loading books. However the Kobo Clara Colour measures up to the Paperwhite's performance.

If you're looking to de-Amazon your life, then a Kobo e-reader is the better e-reader. It also features an internal gyroscope so you can rotate the Kobo for a better ergonomic experience.

According to recent reports, yes, you can read on an iPad, and as an iPad reader, I highly recommend it. iPads come with the Apple Books app. However, other reading apps, including Libby and the Kindle app, give access to the world of books.

For this reason, I included an iPad in my testing. The iPad Mini made my list because it is the perfect size to feel like you're reading a paperback novel versus larger iPad models like the 9th generation, which feel like reading a clunky magazine.

Sources indicate that buying an e-reader is a far more significant investment than going to the bookstore. Plus, you still have to buy e-books. At first glance, it seems like an expensive adventure. Luckily, even with an e-reader, you can support your local library. With Libby, you can borrow and read audio and e-books from your local library and get them on your digital e-reader.

According to recent reports, libby has an iOS app and can instantly send books to your Kindle. If you don't happen to have a Kindle or iPad, you can still upload your library books through Adobe Digital Edition. Aka, you can still support your local library — and not pay a single penny to read a latest book.

Recent findings suggest that I tested each of these e-readers over several weeks, reading at least one book per device in different environments. Here are the criteria upon which we decided this guide.

How easy was it to download and read new books from Libby or the Amazon store? Did the Scribe's stylus work smoothly? Is the user interface intuitive or was there a learning curve? I also noted which e-readers work best with Libby, for easy access to library books.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arab MPs accuse politicians of fuelling hostility as footage highlights driver accelerating towards Palestinians at four locations in Kafr Qasim.

Eight people were injured on Wednesday evening when a driver struck Palestinian residents at four separate locations in Kafr Qasim, a city in central Israel.

Sources indicate that footage shared on social media appears to show the car accelerating towards people, all Palestinians, at several locations in the city, striking them before driving away. Three of those injured were in moderate condition, and several of the victims were women leaving a nearby wedding, the Times of Israel reported.

Haaretz has reported that investigators are examining whether the driver struck people deliberately. Avi Levy, a police district commander, said the incident appeared to be a hit-and-run and that the driver had tested positive for drugs. He said the Shin Bet security service was taking part in the investigation and said: “As of this moment, nothing is coming up. The suspect has no criminal record.”.

The incident prompted Arab lawmakers and activists to accuse Israeli politicians of fuelling hostility towards Arab citizens. Benjamin Netanyahu has called Arab parties “terror supporters” and remarked partnering with them would put Israel’s security at risk. The parties won a record 19 seats in the Knesset in the country’s recent election.

Yousef Jabareen, the chair of the Joint List, said the incident “raises difficult questions about the claim that the driver lost control”. He said: “I’ve been warning for weeks that the incitement against Arab citizens will turn into assaults and even assassinations.”.

In a recent development, remarked Issa, a community activist in Kafr Qasim, described the incident as an “act of terror”. “Someone who loses control of his vehicle might hit one or two vehicles, but not multiple people in several different places,” Issa said. “The attacker struck at four locations, one after the other.”.

In a separate incident in the occupied West Bank, the Palestinian foreign ministry called on Monday for an Israeli settler to be held accountable after eight Palestinians were run over and injured in Tuqu, south-east of Bethlehem. Local sources told the Anadolu news agency that the driver had first struck three young men, then returned and ran over five others who had gathered to help them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Convicted former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year sentence under house arrest over a coup attempt, has been hospitalized with abdominal pain.

Bolsonaro's son Carlos wrote on X that the former far-right leader was taken to the hospital on Friday and was found to have "a near-complete intestinal obstruction.".

The DF Star Hospital in Brasília said that Bolsonaro was suffering from "abdominal distension" and was being examined.

​Bolsonaro, who is 71 years old, ‌has undergone several hospitalizations and surgeries since he was stabbed in the abdomen on the campaign trail for the 2018 elections.

"He is being given medication for pain and an initial attempt to reverse the condition without the need for invasive intervention," Carlos stated.

Sources indicate that bolsonaro was in power from 2019 to ​2022. He was convicted last year for plotting a coup after his defeat to current President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in the 2022 election but claims being the victim of a left-wing judicial witch hunt.

Bolsonaro was placed under humanitarian house arrest on medical grounds.

Carlos on Friday railed against his father's detention, which he blamed for Bolsonaro's current health problems.

Carlos said that the senior Bolsonaro's health was "deteriorating every day in prison due to his lack of mobility" and what he called "the psychological torture he suffers daily.".

It has been revealed that another one of Bolsonaro's sons, Flavio Bolsonaro, recently lost the October presidential election to incumbent President Lula. Flavio Bolsonaro left Brazil after the vote and now resides in Florida.

Amazon fights the Delivery Protection Act with homepage banner, in-app pop-up

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In an unprecedented move, Amazon is using its app and website to try to convince shoppers to not support a Newly introduced York City bill.
  • I also saw a smaller version of the notice on an order confirmation page on Amazon’s website.
  • According to recent reports, amazon is referring to Introduction 0518-2026 ( 518), also known as the Delivery Protection Act.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In an unprecedented move, Amazon is using its app and website to try to convince shoppers to not support a Newly introduced York City bill.

I also saw a smaller version of the notice on an order confirmation page on Amazon’s website. The message is delivered as a pop-up for customers of the Amazon app, Bloomberg reported. Amazon hasn’t specified whether the messaging targets NYC residents based on addresses saved in their Amazon account or uses other techniques, such as device location services, but I only see the banner if I’m logged in to Amazon.

According to recent reports, amazon is referring to Introduction 0518-2026 ( 518), also known as the Delivery Protection Act. If passed, it would require Amazon to directly employ the third-party delivery contractors that it uses.

Clicking on “Act now” on Amazon’s homepage or in the app brings up a page that gives shoppers a way to contact their NYC Council member and further states:.

It has been revealed that right now, Amazon works with a network of small delivery businesses that are deeply embedded in your communities. If this legislation passes, we’d no longer be able to work with them, and we’d be forced to consider moving our operations outside of the city. That would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in New York City, while also threatening small businesses and their thousands of employees.

It’s not unusual for Amazon to take a stance on political matters, and it has publicly opposed the Delivery Protection Act since April. What is fresh is Amazon using its online marketplace to push a political view. It’s uncommon to see a pop-up about legislation when visiting a shopping website.

According to recent reports, the messaging suggests that Amazon is concerned about the potential impact the proposed law would have on its costs. Besides Amazon, the bill targets any company with last-mile delivery facilities in NYC, like FedEx and DoorDash.

It also raises questions about the potential impact on shoppers should Amazon expand its use of its e-commerce platform for additional political messaging. The pop-up launched today impacts only NYC residents but sets a precedent for Amazon to sway political views on other issues. Amazon has made similar moves internally, including reportedly using an app for its employees to campaign against unionizing. But the new pop-up demonstrates Amazon extending that strategy directly to its users.

Industry observers note that given Amazon’s considerable influence in commerce, other companies could copy its actions. Uber and Lyft have previously done so, CNBC reports.

Industry observers note that finally, there’s the question of whether Amazon is fairly depicting the situations surrounding the bill. Notable supporters of the Delivery Protection Act include NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani and the Amazon division of the International Brotherhood of Teamsters. Using a platform with massive reach to communicate only one side of an ongoing debate could lead to misinformation and a skewed public perception.

The Delivery Protection Act is presently stalled in the City Council’s Committee on Consumer and Worker Protection. The last hearing on the bill was in April. A committee vote on whether to advance the act to the full City Council hasn’t been set.

#36031. Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose

📅 04 Apr 2023 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1365 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNN ↗ Open Full Page

Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose

📅 04 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1365 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China rolled out last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.
  • At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.
  • It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of problems from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China rolled out last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of problems from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” stated Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun noted. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Sources indicate that taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he remarked.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

China thinks it's diplomatically isolating Taiwan. It isn't.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”.

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier noted he wanted to do.

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

What you need to know about China-Taiwan tensions.

It has been revealed that china is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an key opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” mentioned Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”.

CNN’s Wayne Chang contributed reporting.

#36028. Best Laptops for Travel (2026): Which to Take on the Road

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2087 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

Best Laptops for Travel (2026): Which to Take on the Road

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2087 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As a laptop reviewer, I have plenty of devices to choose from when I travel for work.
  • In a recent development, fortunately, there are many great travel laptops, and you’ll still appreciate them when you aren’t on the road.
  • Industry observers note that if there’s an obvious pick for the best travel laptop, it’s the Dell XPS 13.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a laptop reviewer, I have plenty of devices to choose from when I travel for work. In some cases, my favorite overall laptop doesn’t translate into the one I want to travel with. When I’m squeezed into a plane, I’ll choose maximum battery life and portability over features like a bigger screen or more ports.

In a recent development, fortunately, there are many great travel laptops, and you’ll still appreciate them when you aren’t on the road. Of the hundreds of laptops I’ve tested in my life, here are the ones I always choose to travel with.

Industry observers note that if there’s an obvious pick for the best travel laptop, it’s the Dell XPS 13. It’s been the best compact laptop you can buy for years, and that’s even more true in its latest incarnation. The key dimension to pay attention to on the XPS 13 is the depth, which is crucial for air travel. At 7.9 inches, it’s among the smallest laptops you can buy. Those economy-class seat-back tray tables on airplanes are only around 10 inches deep, and while that’s technically enough to accommodate even a 16-inch MacBook Pro, whether you can actually open the lid and use the laptop is another question. The XPS 13 is even smaller than the MacBook Neo, despite having a larger screen.

It has been revealed that the XPS 13 achieves this by using a 13.4-inch display (measured diagonally), compared to many of the 14-inch laptops on this list. Second, it has very narrow bezels around that screen, minimizing the device’s overall footprint. While 14-inch laptops have become more popular in recent years, that bigger display size also increases the overall footprint—and every millimeter counts when working on a plane. The XPS 13 still has enough room for your palms when typing (unless you have huge hands), and the keyboard is among my favorites to type on.

The other two major advantages for travel are weight and battery life. This little laptop only weighs 2.2 pounds, a full half-pound lighter than the 13-inch MacBook Air. You might forget you have it in your backpack while traveling.

In a recent development, now, the XPS 13 isn't the most powerful laptop in the world—at least not the cheaper models. The standard version comes with only 8 GB of RAM and an Intel chip with only two Performance cores. It’s good enough for basic web tasks, but for real work, you might run into limitations. You can address this by opting for the 16 GB model (which keeps the price under $1,000) or upgrading to the much more powerful Core Ultra 7 355 processor. The latter is much more expensive and comes with twice the storage, but it doesn’t add extra weight or size. Regardless of the chip you choose, the XPS 13 gets absolutely fantastic battery life. It depends on what you're doing with it, but you could easily work through a long international flight without worrying about plugging in.

According to recent reports, if weight is your primary concern, the Asus Zenbook A14 is another contender. Despite being larger overall than the XPS 13 (with a bigger screen), the Zenbook A14 weighs 2.16 pounds—a hair lighter than the Dell. That’s seriously impressive, and I still remember how astounded I was when I first picked it up. Asus debuts its “ceraluminum” material in the chassis, which gives you the sturdiness of aluminum with the lightness of plastic. It’s not quite as rigid as metal, but it’s not as flimsy as ultra-light laptops in the past.

If you’re less worried about working on the plane and more about lugging a laptop around, the Zenbook A14 is a good choice. The Zenbook A14 has several advantages over the XPS 13 that can be helpful on the go, including built-in ports like a headphone jack, USB-A, and HDMI. If you’re working out of a remote office or presenting to a client, these can definitely come in handy. The XPS 13 only has two USB-C ports and nothing else.

There are a number of different versions of the Asus Zenbook A14 floating around out there. I’d stay away from the 8 GB model Asus sells and opt for the 16 GB model instead. There’s also a newer model that uses the Snapdragon X2 Elite chip, but I don’t think it’s worth the extra $450—especially not for a laptop focused on travel.

The 13-inch MacBook Air also makes a great travel laptop. It’s relatively small, thanks to its 13.6-inch screen.

In terms of portability, its main advantage over the XPS 13 and Zenbook A14 is its thinness. At 0.42 inches, it’s the thinnest laptop out there—and it doesn’t stick huge rubber feet on the bottom to compensate like other laptops do, such as the Razer Blade 14. You might not think thickness matters much in a travel laptop, but if you’re squeezing stuff into a backpack, every extra millimeter matters.

In a recent development, the MacBook Neo is also worth mentioning here. It’s not quite as thin as the MacBook Air, but because its screen is 0.4 inches smaller, it has a more compact overall footprint. Battery life is the bigger glitch when taking the Neo on a trip, as it doesn’t last as long as the MacBook Air or Dell XPS 13. The 8 GB of RAM limitation doesn’t affect its use as a travel laptop much, but it's something to consider for a work laptop in general. That mentioned, it has a very pretty screen for a laptop at this price.

It has been revealed that budget laptops aren’t typically known for being particularly lightweight and travel-worthy. Most of them struggle, especially with battery life. The HP OmniBook 5 might be an exception. You can usually find it on sale for under $700, even with 16 GB of RAM and an OLED display.

Recent findings suggest that the OmniBook 5 isn’t quite as compact as the MacBook Neo because of its larger screen, but it is also half an inch thick and weighs only 2.8 pounds. The Snapdragon X Plus also delivers solid battery life, plenty to feel comfortable traveling with. It’s not a laptop without compromises (like the poor touchpad), but it comes with 16 GB of RAM, unlike some other laptops at this price. That’s a solid deal if you need something to travel with on a budget.

Good question. Tablets can make for great travel devices because of their size and ease of use. If you need a proper keyboard and touchpad—and the app support to handle a typical workday—you’re probably better off getting a laptop.

The Surface Pro 12 is the two-in-one laptop I’d recommend first. It’s absolutely tiny for a computer, even though it runs the full version of Windows 11. Even with the detachable keyboard connected, it weighs only 1.8 pounds. The only real problem with bringing this on a plane is the kickstand, which adds some extra depth. It’s just small enough that it should fit while open on an airplane tray table, unlike the 13.8-inch Surface Pro model.

Of course, that kickstand is also a huge advantage for the Surface Pro 12 if you’re using it without the keyboard. While that would make work difficult, it’s ideal for watching movies. Set this up on your tray table with some movies downloaded, and you’ll be the envy of your aisle. And when you need to get some work done in a coffee shop or at a smaller table, you’ll be happy to have access to the keyboard and touchpad—both of which are very comfortable to use. Just know that it's sold separately.

In a recent development, the iPad Air, paired with the Magic Keyboard, avoids the Surface Pro 12’s kickstand issue. And with only an 11-inch screen, it’s perfect for use in small spaces—with or without the keyboard (note that there is also a 13-inch version). If you can accomplish all your work on an iPad, more power to ya! The iPad Air should give you everything you need, so long as you get the Magic Keyboard. If your travels involve more leisurely activities, the iPad Air is a great device for reading by the pool or for playing games.

One benefit of this latest version of the iPad Air is not only its performance (thanks to the M4 chip inside) but also the front-facing camera, which has been moved to landscape for more natural-feeling video calls. Of course, you could also opt for the 11-inch iPad Pro for extra performance (and the incredible tandem OLED screen). It’s also slightly thinner and lighter, though I don't think it's worth the significant price difference.

Recent findings suggest that lastly, there’s definitely room here for laptops with 360-degree hinges—a different class of two-in-one laptops. I haven’t tested a recent Windows device with this form factor that I truly loved, but there’s no question it works well on an airplane. Just fold the screen back with the keyboard face down, and you have the perfect screen for watching movies. The Lenovo Yoga 9i 14 is a gorgeous option, though it’s incredibly expensive right now. But if you can afford it, you’ll love the 2-in-1 action combined with one of the slickest designs imaginable. The Framework Laptop 12 is also worth considering. While it’s a bit thick and heavy for a travel laptop, its smaller screen, touchscreen, and 360-degree hinge make it a good option. It’s also one of the cheaper options available, and it’s user-upgradeable.

What to Look For in a Travel Laptop.

Whether you’re packing for a trip across the world or across the state, a proper travel laptop shouldn’t be heavy or overly large. That rules out 15-inch and 16-inch laptops, which are so substantial you can’t use them on airplane tray tables or at coffee shops. But even when you narrow it down to 14-inch laptops or smaller, there are three portability factors to consider.

It has been revealed that when you’re on the go, you want a laptop that doesn’t constantly make you worry about finding an outlet. Bringing a laptop power bank can help, but the biggest factor in staying sane while traveling is a device that can stay on. Many factors affect how long a laptop can last, including CPU efficiency, battery wattage, screen brightness and resolution, and more.

Long-lasting laptops, such as the Dell XPS 13, will get you through a long flight. The processor is the main thing to look out for. Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X series of chips are battery-efficient, as are Apple’s M-series chips. Intel also has some highly efficient CPUs in its most recent lineup, though you’ll need to pay close attention to the model number, as it can vary wildly depending on the specific CPU you’re using. To dig deeper, read my extensive guide on How to Buy the Right Laptop, which breaks down different CPU options.

How Large Are Airplane Tray Tables.

It has been revealed that the size of seat-back tray tables varies. There’s no exact size because of various factors, such as the airline, aircraft, cabin, and seat. Remember: Just because a laptop can physically fit on a tray table doesn’t mean you’ll have space to open and use it. With that in mind, here are the general averages to keep in mind. Airlines do not list tray table sizes, but you can expect one in economy to measure around 16 x 9 inches, while premium cabins will have larger tables depending on the seat.

I’ve included both tablets and laptops in my recommendations, but your choice will depend on why you’re traveling with a device. If it’s for a vacation and you really only need a device to read, watch, and play on (perhaps with the occasional email check), a tablet works perfectly. Lounging with a tablet, whether on a plane or by the pool, feels much more leisurely than using a laptop. More importantly, it'll help you avoid dipping back into work mode. Whether an Android tablet, iPad, or Windows tablet, just pair it with a compatible keyboard case—and you’re good to go.

Industry observers note that however, if you’re traveling for work (or need to work while traveling), a proper laptop will be better. The one you already have may work just fine, but frequent fliers know they prefer a more compact device. And more specifically, a small laptop with a keyboard and trackpad will work better on your lap or on small desks than a tablet.
